newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND SKIPS GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND SKIPS GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: French speed racer Luc Alphand stayed in bed rather than risk embarrassment in Saturday's giant slalom, leaving the outcome of the World Cup overall title in the hands of Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt.
Alphand, against his own wishes, was made a surprise entry on the start list by French coaches for the first leg of the final giant slalom of the season.

But the 31-year-old Frenchman, who had not competed in a technical event in six years, did not show up for the race, but hopes that his 106-point lead over Aamodt will stand up after the weekend's two technical races.
"Luc is at the hotel in bed and is watching on TV," said Alphand's manager, Ralf Krieger.

"He will come to watch the second leg," added Krieger, who said Alphand did not get back to his hotel until 3 a.m. after attending a Colorado Avalanche-Pittsburgh Penguins ice hockey game on Friday night in Denver.
Alphand had been resigned to playing a waiting game in the chase for the World Cup overall crown after he was through with the downhill and Super-G speed events at the Finals.
He reacted angrily on Friday to word that team coaches were considering entering him in the giant slalom as a psychological ploy against Aamodt, who is second in giant slalom standings.
"I haven't made a zig-zag for six years and I don't want to be a clown," Alphand said before heading to Denver for the National Hockey League game.

Alphand had the option to race despite being outside the top 25 racers that qualified for the World Cup Finals based on points. Skiers with at least 400 overall points are eligible to enter any of the finals.
